verdicts.evidence: docker logs --since 24h on 10.10.60.14, per worker '<n> search, <m> cards' summaries vs '0 cards': w1 40/0, w3 78/4, w4 35/0, w5 367/276, w6 36/1, w7 39/2, w8 0/0, w9 0/0, w10 35/1, so 284/630 = 45%. Worker-5 lines read 'No listings found for "ssd lot server ssd samsung micron" within 40 miles' after 'with radius=100'; the next line is ERROR [Search] Failed to get search results; still recurring (18 in the last 2h). Workers 1/3/4/6/7/10 get 110-120 cards per search on the same queries with radius=100.
verdicts.reason: The 45% figure reproduces, but the diagnosis is wrong. 276 of the 284 empty searches come from one worker, rs-fleet-worker-60-14-5; the other workers run the same queries at radius=100 and get full pages, so this is neither a fleet-wide radius bug nor a too-narrow query. It is worker-5's account or session state. Each empty task finishes in about 8 s, so worker-5 claims about 58% of the host's tasks and wastes them, which keeps it a real P2 for search budget. Fix: detect a worker whose searches return '0 cards' repeatedly and park it, rather than changing radius or queries. Inspecting that account's session is owner-only (see needs_owner).

verdicts.reason: Blocked runs that report SUCCEEDED, and the missing origin/dev, both reproduce. 'Since at least 2026-07-14' was not verified: the run's own count starts at 10-27. The same run fetched origin/inspection-reports fine, so an explicit 'git fetch origin dev' would fix the base problem; it is a prompt gap, not a hard block. What is left is a monitoring gap the owner is already told about every night, so P3.
